# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 16:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 199 active entries of tips_notebook.json (26 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

Kill the most-accused claimant only when the Village has no checkable result on them. Each night we killed the loudest claimant, and the Village's Lookout-versus-Lookout fight kept the real information unresolved. Keep a pre-agreed rule for choosing targets so the team doesn't drift.

A self-nominating player who keeps saying they are a 'fair target' is often a Jester. Quietly nudge the Village toward hanging that player, since a Jester hang wins for them and the Yakuza lose no one. Don't push that nudge too hard, or it reads as Yakuza steering.

A Medic self-protect with a Standard token explains a Standard-level survivor. Before voting, ask the survivor directly for the attack type and whether they were protected. Silence after that question is weak evidence, so don't hang on silence alone when a clear claim is available.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night.
tips_feedback.why: The team voted identically every night, so the Katana kill chain (Grace, Bob, Carol, Heidi) worked without mismatches or exposure.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them.
tips_feedback.why: We kept day coordination in public or in the night chat only, so no team private messages were exposed or misread.

tips_feedback.tip: Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover.
tips_feedback.why: Erin said she could not confirm or deny the Carol visit instead of denying it, which kept her credible while Ivan's claim stayed unverified.

lessons.tip: Ignite as soon as 2 or 3 doused players are still alive and a Strong ignite would kill a real threat. Dousing night after night without igniting let the Yakuza pick the kills and got me hanged on Day 4 with zero kills.

Don't switch a survival story under trial pressure. My innate-Defense explanation was replaced by a Medic claim when hanging was near, and the table read the switch as a lie. Choose one story early or stay quiet.

Watch for Jester tells: a player who pushes a Yes on a rival, then self-nominates and repeatedly says they are a fair target or won't object is often a Jester seeking a hang. Test that pattern before following the crowd.

Track which claimants the Katana hits each night. The Yakuza kept one holder and targeted the most active claimants, so a claimant who dies to the Katana is likely real, while a claimant who survives is worth a visit-based test.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: The advice was accurate. I doused Bob, Carol and Erin across three nights without igniting and was hanged on Day 4 with no kills, so I failed to follow it.

tips_feedback.tip: A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Survival was my Arsonist innate Defense, not Medic protection. The table treated my survival as evidence for a Medic claim, and that claim was a false story that backfired when the trial read it as a lie.

lessons.tip: Unspent shot tokens are worth nothing. Yakuza kill the last unexplained non-Yakuza player with the Katana, so spend a shot on the strongest mechanical lead before the Katana reaches you rather than holding all three for a lead that never comes.

Two players claiming the same role is a conflict, but a claimed result with no night or detail is not yet a contradiction. Ask once for the specifics, then move to checkable visits and vote records instead of repeating demands for days.

Surviving a Katana hit can come from protection or innate Defense (Arsonist and Serial Killer have Standard Defense). Treat a survivor's claim as a test to check, not as proof they are a real Medic or other Village role.

Track who benefits from each nomination and kill. Yakuza pushed silence-based nominations against Village claimants, and the Village hanged or lost several of its own claimants that way. Before voting, ask whether the vote helps the Yakuza.
Repeated 'no new result, still no nomination' messages burn budget and add nothing. Spend the budget on one concrete check or contradiction per round so the table has something to vote on.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots.
tips_feedback.why: I followed it and never fired. No clean mechanical lead appeared while the Yakuza killed one Village player per night, and I died on Night 4 with all 3 tokens unspent, so the caution gave the Village no kill.

tips_feedback.tip: A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Grace survived a Standard hit through her Arsonist innate Defense, and her Medic claim was false. Survival alone does not establish a real claim.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: My pressure on Grace's unexplained Standard-level Defense as a possible Arsonist or Serial Killer was correct; she was the Arsonist.

lessons.tip: A lone Lookout claim with one visitor, denied by that visitor and unconfirmed, becomes a lynch target. Post the full result with night and visitor list once, then point to contradictions in other claims. Repeating a demand for the night every round reads as stalling and gets you nominated.

A player who self-nominates while saying 'I won't object' or 'I'm a fair target' may be a Jester seeking a hang. Hanging them wins them the game, so before a Guilty majority, check whether the nominee wins by being hanged and consider a different action.

Keep the Katana with one holder who never claims or draws attention, and make no daytime PMs between teammates. Target claimants whose results conflict with yours, and let the Village argue over unverifiable claims while you vote the same way every night.

Each round, post one new check, such as a new contradiction or a direct question with a deadline. Repeating the same accusation or 'not nominating yet' costs budget and makes your messages look like filler.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: No daytime PMs between teammates; every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza kept all coordination in the night chat and never sent a daytime PM between teammates, so no PM cluster tied them together while the Village argued about Carol's and Bob's PMs.

tips_feedback.tip: Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority.
tips_feedback.why: Frank applied the Jester check to Alice, found the pattern suspicious, and still voted Guilty, which won Alice the game. The check was right but the response was wrong: the Village should have abstained or redirected instead of hanging the likely Jester.

lessons.tip: A player who pushes a Yes on a Village-looking nominee, then nominates themself and says they are a fair target who won't object, may be a Jester. Before any hang on pressure, check whether the nominee wins by being hanged, because the Jester won this game that way.

When Yakuza are a minority of the living, count the exact Guilty majority needed before the vote. Let Village players make the public case against a Village nominee and keep Yakuza Guilty votes aligned with the visible majority, so the Yakuza bloc never stands out.

After a Katana hit fails, switch targets rather than repeating the same kill. A self-protecting Medic is hard to see from the outside, and a survivor's claim can come out later and reshape the Village vote.

Do not hold the rig as a backup token until the end. Spend it on a Day when the Village would otherwise fail to execute a Village player, because an unused token does nothing once the game is decided.

Repeated demands for the same answer, like naming a night, spend budget without adding information. Short posts that name one concrete contradiction are more useful in later rounds where the multiplier is higher.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: Yakuza kept targets in the night chat only, so the Village never had a public target to read or pre-empt before each kill.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them.
tips_feedback.why: Yakuza coordinated only in the night chat and kept the daytime clean, so no PM link tied Erin, Frank and Judy together during the Village's PM-based suspicion.

summary: The Yakuza (Erin Ritualist, Frank Smuggler, Judy Clerk) won without using a single role ability. They kept the Katana on Erin, killed an information role each night and voted with the Village crowd. The Village beat itself in three ways. (1) Day 2 went to two Lookout claims. Ivan was really a Roleplayer and Bob the real Lookout. The table settled it with a bogus 'name the night' demand, even though only Night 1 had passed. Nobody used Carol's archive list, which showed both Lookout and Roleplayer and so explained the double claim without anyone being Evil. Hanging Ivan was harmless, but the Yakuza then killed Bob for free. (2) Day 3: Alice was the Jester. She kept calling herself a 'fair target' and then nominated herself. The table hanged her 6-2. Frank had openly named the Jester read and still voted Guilty. Her revenge killed Dave, the Profiler. His two profiles of Carol had both shown Archivist, and their decoy roles (Smuggler, Ritualist) proved Yakuza roles were in play. (3) Day 4, at 5 alive with 3 Yakuza: Grace, an Arsonist, first said 'innate Defense' and then switched to a Medic claim mid-trial. She was hanged with three players doused and never ignited. Heidi, the Vigilante, never fired a shot in three nights and died with every token. Erin, Frank and Judy were never nominated: they never sent each other a daytime PM and always echoed the consensus.

lessons.tip: A player who self-nominates, keeps saying 'I'm a fair target / I won't object', or begs to be hanged without a claim is very likely a Jester. Vote No on the nomination and Innocent at trial. A Jester hang wastes the Day and its revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
lessons.evidence: Alice repeated 'I'm a fair target' for two Days, then nominated herself. She was hanged 6-2 and her revenge Divine Attack killed Dave, the Profiler. Frank, a Yakuza, had openly called the Jester read and still voted Guilty.

lessons.tip: When two players claim the same investigative role and one result is unverifiable, check for a Roleplayer before calling it a Yakuza lie. If an Archivist, Profiler or Surveyor result shows 'Roleplayer', the duplicate claimant with the oddest result is probably it. Discount that player's results instead of spending the Day hanging them.
lessons.evidence: Carol's archive showed both Lookout and Roleplayer. Ivan, a Roleplayer with fake role Lookout, got a false 'Carol visited Erin' result. Carol even said 'liar or Roleplayer' once. Yet the table spent all of Day 2 on Ivan, and the Yakuza killed Bob, the real Lookout, that night.

lessons.tip: Check that a 'contradiction' is real before using it to hang someone. Repeating an impossible demand creates false certainty and burns budget. Use your messages to share results and do role math, not to echo the same question.
lessons.evidence: For dozens of messages, players demanded Ivan 'name the night' of his Erin result when only Night 1 had passed. Heidi was the only one who pointed this out. 'Grace, name the hit' was also repeated for rounds by nearly everyone. Meanwhile nobody analyzed the archive list.

lessons.tip: Use your shots before the Yakuza reach parity. Holding all tokens is the same as being a Vanilla Villager. Mid-game, a Basic shot on the most suspicious claimless voice is worth the risk. Good targets are players who push nominations on 'silence' or always echo the consensus.
lessons.evidence: Heidi took no action on Nights 1, 2 and 3 and died on Night 4 with every token. That left the Yakuza 3 of 5 on Day 4 with nothing to slow them. Judy had led weak nominations of Carol and Grace and would have been a reasonable shot.

lessons.tip: Profile decoys are drawn from roles actually in play, so publish all three names. Evil roles among them (Smuggler, Ritualist, Arsonist) tell the table what threats exist. Overlap across two profiles narrows the true role. Post each result in your will at once, and profile unclaimed players rather than re-testing an active claimant.
lessons.evidence: Dave profiled Carol twice: Archivist/Arsonist/Smuggler, then Archivist/Ritualist/Smuggler. Both lists named Yakuza roles present in the game. The second result never reached the table because Dave died that night. Erin, Frank and Judy, all unclaimed, were never profiled.

lessons.tip: If you survive an attack with innate Defense, prepare one consistent cover claim before you're pressured. Switching stories mid-trial is fatal. Once three or more players are doused and you're under suspicion, ignite rather than waiting to be hanged.
lessons.evidence: Grace said 'innate Defense, nobody protected me', then switched to a Medic self-protect claim on trial and was hanged 3-2. Carol, Erin and earlier Bob had all been doused, but she never ignited and died with zero kills.

lessons.tip: Quiet, consistent play wins. Agree on Katana votes every night, send no daytime PMs to teammates, and echo the Village's own reasoning instead of leading. Let the Village spend its hangs on Neutrals or Roleplayers. Kill information roles and avoid players who already survived a hit.
lessons.evidence: Erin, Frank and Judy sent no daytime PMs, avoided Grace after Night 1, and killed Bob, Carol and Heidi. They joined the Ivan, Alice and Grace hangs on the crowd's own arguments. None of them was ever nominated or even seriously suspected.

lessons.tip: Once an Archivist list is public, do slot math. Match claims to listed roles and flag listed Evil roles (Clerk, Ritualist) as live threats. The players who never claim anything are where those roles hide.
lessons.evidence: Carol's list included Clerk and Ritualist, and both were real (Judy, Erin). No one ever asked who among the non-claimers (Erin, Frank, Judy, Heidi, Alice) could fill those slots. The three Yakuza simply stayed 'no role claim' all game.

tips_feedback.tip: Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff).
tips_feedback.why: The warning was correct, but the Village ignored it. It hanged self-nominating Alice, a Jester, and her revenge killed Dave. Frank, a Yakuza, even named the Jester read aloud while voting Guilty.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips).
tips_feedback.why: Players kept quoting the 'contradiction' standard but filled it with a fake one: Ivan's 'no night named' when only one night existed. They also stalled for rounds demanding 'visit-based contradictions' instead of analyzing the archive list.

tips_feedback.tip: PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead.
tips_feedback.why: The Carol-Bob PMs were both Village, yet they became the main suspicion thread. Judy nominated Carol over them, and the Yakuza openly chose Bob as a 'PM hub' kill. The real Yakuza bloc avoided PMs entirely.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes).
tips_feedback.why: With flips hidden and few hard leads, Heidi read this as 'never shoot'. She died on Night 4 with all tokens unused while the Yakuza reached a majority.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent zero daytime PMs to each other and voted in unison every night. No PM pattern ever linked them, and the Village's PM suspicion fell on Carol and Bob instead.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: After the Night 1 Katana failed on Grace (an Arsonist with Standard Defense), the Yakuza never retried her. They switched to killable information roles and got a kill every remaining night.

tips_feedback.tip: If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged.
tips_feedback.why: Grace did the opposite. She went from 'innate Defense, nobody protected me' to a Medic claim mid-trial and was hanged 3-2, which confirms the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected.
tips_feedback.why: Grace ignored it. Bob, Carol and Erin had all been doused, and she was nominated on Day 4 without ever igniting, dying with no kills, as the tip warns.

issues.description: On Day 2 many players (Bob, Dave, Alice, Heidi, Judy and others) kept pressing Erin to confirm or deny whether Carol visited her, as if targets learn their visitors. No rule tells a player who visited them; Erin correctly said she couldn't see visitors. Several players also treated Erin's non-confirmation as evidence against Ivan's claim.

For most of Day 2, nearly every player demanded that Ivan 'name the night' of his Erin result, though only Night 1 had happened and Ivan had said N1 from his first claim. In the trial, Dave and Frank said Ivan had 'had three Days' to answer, but it was the first Day (Day 2). Only Heidi pointed out the error. This misreading of the game timeline helped hang Ivan.

Several players (Carol, Ivan, Alice, Bob) reported in mid-game feedback that by the late rounds of Day 2 a public message cost more than their remaining budget. Bob said a nomination (3.50 of 4.22) left too little to explain it. The prompt apparently does not show the cheapest public message price or the remaining budget clearly enough to plan around this. Frank also reported he could not see his remaining speaking budget.
Frank (Smuggler) reported after the game that the night prompt did not clearly offer the Smuggler swap option, so the action interface for that role may be unclear.

Under the secret-vote setting, the log records only trial totals, not the individual Guilty votes. That makes Alice's Jester revenge, which must hit a random Guilty voter, impossible to audit. The revenge hit Dave, who had publicly said he was leaning Innocent on Alice. It cannot be checked from the log whether Dave actually voted Guilty.

Ivan and Heidi described Carol and Bob as having 'sent each other' private messages, and Heidi said Bob PM'd Carol. In fact only Carol sent PMs to Bob, and the public PM notices showed the direction. This misreading of the private-message notifications fed suspicion of Bob.
